questtg1-parents#7.en: Cosine starts at its peak (at 0°); sine starts at 0 and rises; tangent has vertical asymptotes.

questtg1-parents#9.en: What is the period of y = ${fn} x?

questtg1-parents#10.en: The period is one full cycle. Sine & cosine repeat every 360°; tangent every 180°.

questtg1-parents#14.en: What is the range of y = ${fn} x?

questtg1-parents#17.en: Sine & cosine stay between −1 and 1. Tangent reaches every real value.

questtg1-parents#20.en: What is the amplitude of y = ${fn} x?

questtg1-parents#21.en: Amplitude is the height from the middle to a peak. Tangent has no peak, so it is undefined.

questtg1-parents#24.en: Where are the asymptotes of y = tan x for x ∈ [0° ; 360°]?

questtg1-parents#29.en: tan x = sin x ÷ cos x. The graph is undefined where cos x = 0.

questtg1-parents#32.en: The peak is the highest point — where the graph reaches +1.

questtg1-parents#33.en: The peak of y = ${fn} x is at (${peakX}° ; 1).

questtg1-parents#34.en: y = ${fn} x reaches its maximum of 1 at x = ${peakX}°.

questtg2-params#4.en: Reflects the graph in the x-axis (flips it upside-down)

questtg2-params#8.en: A negative a only flips the graph over the x-axis; it does not move it or change the period.

questtg2-params#9.en: A negative a reflects the graph in the x-axis.

questtg2-params#10.en: Compared with y = ${fn} x, the graph ${eqStr(cv)} is…

questtg2-params#15.en: a stretches the graph vertically — it sets the amplitude (the height to a peak).

questtg2-params#18.en: Squashes it sideways → ${b} cycles in 360° (shorter period)

questtg2-params#22.en: b changes the period: period = 360° ÷ b. A bigger b means more cycles squeezed into 360°.

questtg2-params#26.en: How is ${eqStr(cv)} different from y = ${fn} x?

questtg2-params#31.en: q slides the whole graph vertically. q > 0 up, q < 0 down. The midline becomes y = q.

questtg2-params#36.en: The midline runs through the middle of the wave at y = q (the dashed line).

questtg2-params#38.en: Is ${eqStr(cv)} the graph of y = ${fn} x reflected in the x-axis?

questtg2-params#39.en: A reflection in the x-axis flips the graph upside-down — that happens when a is negative.

questtg2-params#40.en: Yes — a = −1 flips y = ${fn} x in the x-axis.

questtg2-params#41.en: No — a = 1, so it is just y = ${fn} x (not flipped).

questtg2-params#42.en: a is negative, so the graph is reflected in the x-axis.

questtg2-params#43.en: a is positive, so the graph is the normal way up.

questtg3-period-amp-range#2.en: Period = ${base}° ÷ b. ${fn === "tan" ? "Tangent uses 180°." : "Sine and cosine use 360°."}

questtg3-period-amp-range#7.en: Tangent has no maximum or minimum, so it has no amplitude.

questtg3-period-amp-range#9.en: Amplitude = |a| (always positive). The sign of a only flips the graph.

questtg3-period-amp-range#17.en: Range = [q − amplitude ; q + amplitude]. Start at the midline, go one amplitude each way.

questtg3-period-amp-range#21.en:
${eqStr(cv)}
How many complete cycles does this graph make for x ∈ [0° ; 360°]?

questtg3-period-amp-range#22.en: Number of cycles = interval length ÷ period = 360° ÷ period.

questtg3-period-amp-range#25.en: Read the period off the graph. The arrow marks one full cycle.

questtg3-period-amp-range#26.en: The period is the width of one complete wave (peak to the next peak).

questtg3-period-amp-range#28.en: Read the amplitude off the graph (use the marked peak and trough).

questtg3-period-amp-range#29.en: Amplitude = (y max − y min) ÷ 2. Read y max and y min off the y-axis (the dashed guides).

questtg3-period-amp-range#31.en: Read the range off the graph (the marked peak and trough).

questtg3-period-amp-range#32.en: Range = from the lowest y-value (trough) up to the highest (peak).

questtg3-period-amp-range#34.en: Amplitude needs a highest and lowest point. Tangent has neither.

questtg3-period-amp-range#35.en: No — tangent has no maximum or minimum, so its amplitude is undefined.

questtg3-period-amp-range#36.en: tan climbs without bound between its asymptotes, so there is no peak or trough — no amplitude.

questtg4-shifts#10.en: The bracket is (x − p). The graph moves the OPPOSITE way to the sign: (x − 30°) → right, (x + 30°) → left.

questtg4-shifts#12.en: Which equation shifts y = ${fn} x ${mag}° to the left?

questtg4-shifts#15.en: Left means the bracket reads (x + …). A vertical (+ outside the function) does not move it sideways.

questtg4-shifts#17.en: f = sin x and g = cos x are drawn. How must y = ${from} x be shifted to give y = ${to} x?

questtg4-shifts#22.en: Cosine peaks at 0°, sine only at 90° — cosine is 90° 'ahead'. Slide the peaks onto each other.

questtg4-shifts#23.en: cos x = sin(x + 90°): shift sin x 90° left.

questtg4-shifts#24.en: sin x = cos(x − 90°): shift cos x 90° right.

questtg4-shifts#25.en: sin x peaks at 90°; cos x peaks at 0°

questtg4-shifts#26.en: cos x peaks at 0°; sin x peaks at 90°

questtg4-shifts#27.en: every feature must move 90° left: cos x = sin(x + 90°)

questtg4-shifts#28.en: every feature must move 90° right: sin x = cos(x − 90°)

questtg4-shifts#29.en: Rewrite y = ${fn}(${b}x − ${inner}°) as y = ${fn} b(x − p). What is the real horizontal shift?

questtg4-shifts#34.en: Factor b out: ${fn}(${b}x − ${inner}°) = ${fn} ${b}(x − ${shift}°). The shift is ${shift}°, not ${inner}°.

questtg4-shifts#39.en:
${eqStr(cv)}
How is it shifted from y = ${fn} x?

questtg4-shifts#44.en: q is added outside the function, so it slides the graph vertically (+ up, − down).

questtg4-shifts#46.en: Start with y = ${a}${fn} x, then shift it ${Math.abs(q)} ${q > 0 ? "up" : "down"}. What is the new range?

questtg4-shifts#48.en: Amplitude stays ${A}; the midline moves to y = ${nstr(q)}. Range = [${nstr(q - A)} ; ${nstr(q + A)}].

questtg4-shifts#50.en: Does shifting a graph left, right, up or down change its period?

questtg4-shifts#51.en: Only b changes the period. Shifting just slides the same wave to a new place.

questtg4-shifts#52.en: No — shifts move the graph but the period (set by b) stays the same.

questtg4-shifts#53.en: Period = 360° ÷ b. Shifts change p and q, not b, so the period is unchanged.

questtg5-tan#5.en: y = tan x is undefined (has a vertical asymptote) wherever…

questtg5-tan#10.en: tan x = sin x ÷ cos x. A fraction is undefined when its denominator is 0.

questtg5-tan#12.en: What are the x-intercepts of y = tan x for x ∈ [0° ; 360°]?

questtg5-tan#17.en: tan x = 0 where the numerator sin x = 0.

questtg5-tan#24.en: Tangent climbs without bound between its asymptotes, so it reaches every real value.

questtg5-tan#25.en: Range: y ∈ ℝ (any a, b, p, q).

questtg5-tan#26.en: A tan graph crosses its midline at an inflection point. 45° to the right it sits at y = ${nstr(hi)}; 45° to the left it sits at y = ${nstr(lo)}. Find a.

questtg5-tan#27.en: a = (the value 45° right − the value 45° left) ÷ 2.

questtg5-tan#30.en: For a tan graph, does a larger size of a make the branches steeper?

questtg5-tan#31.en: Tangent has no amplitude, but a still stretches it vertically — that makes each branch steeper.

questtg5-tan#32.en: Yes — a bigger a makes a tan graph steeper (it has no amplitude, but a sets the steepness).

questtg5-tan#33.en: a stretches tan vertically: larger a → steeper branches; smaller a → flatter.

questtg6-find-equation#3.en: Is this the graph of sine, cosine or tangent?

questtg6-find-equation#5.en: Cosine starts at a peak (at 0°); sine starts at 0 and rises; tangent has asymptotes.

questtg6-find-equation#7.en:
The graph shows y = a·${fn} x + q.
Read the value of a (watch the sign).

questtg6-find-equation#8.en: a = (y max − y min) ÷ 2, made negative if the graph is flipped (starts the wrong way up).

questtg6-find-equation#10.en:
The graph shows y = a·${fn} x + q.
Read the value of q (the vertical shift).

questtg6-find-equation#11.en: q = (y max + y min) ÷ 2 — the height of the midline (the dashed line).

questtg6-find-equation#13.en:
The graph shows y = a·${fn} bx.
Read the value of b (use the marked cycle to find the period first).

questtg6-find-equation#14.en: First read the period, then b = 360° ÷ period.

questtg6-find-equation#17.en: Find a (height + sign), q (midline) and b (from the period), then read off sin vs cos.

questtg6-find-equation#19.en:
The graph shows y = a·tan bx.
Read the value of b (use the spacing of the asymptotes).

questtg6-find-equation#20.en: Tangent's asymptotes are one period apart. Period = 180° ÷ b, so b = 180° ÷ period.

questtg7-mixed#8.en: Amplitude is the height from the middle to a peak. The taller wave has the larger amplitude.

questtg7-mixed#9.en: ${af > ag ? "f" : "g"} is taller — amplitude ${Math.max(af, ag)} vs ${Math.min(af, ag)}.

questtg7-mixed#10.en: At x = ${X}°, which graph is higher? (f = sin x, g = cos x)

questtg7-mixed#13.en: Read straight up from x on the dashed line — the higher dot is the higher graph.

questtg7-mixed#14.en: At ${X}°, ${fv > gv ? "f = sin" : "g = cos"} is higher.

questtg7-mixed#15.en: For which interval is sin x > 0 on [0° ; 360°]?

questtg7-mixed#20.en: sin x > 0 where the graph is ABOVE the x-axis (between its x-intercepts at 0° and 180°).

questtg7-mixed#22.en: Does the point (${X}° ; ${nstr(Y)}) lie on y = ${fn} x?

questtg7-mixed#23.en: Work out ${fn} ${X}° and compare it with ${nstr(Y)}.

questtg7-mixed#24.en: ${fn} ${X}° = ${nstr(trueY)}, so the point ${Y === trueY ? "does" : "does not"} lie on the graph.

questtg7-mixed#26.en: Tap a point where f(x) = g(x) (the curves cross). f = sin x, g = cos x.

questtg7-mixed#27.en: An intersection is where the two curves meet — the dot that sits on BOTH.

questtg7-mixed#28.en: f = g at x = 45° (where sin x and cos x cross).

questtg7-mixed#29.en: The graphs cross at x = 45°, where sin 45° = cos 45°.

questtg7-mixed#34.en: Describe the transformation from y = ${fn} x to ${eqStr(cv)}.

questtg7-mixed#35.en: Compare amplitude (a), midline (q), orientation (sign of a) and period (b).
